hindi: समाहर्ता के प्रणिधि में जनपद की रक्षा कही जा चुकी है।
english: In the Collector's praṇidhi, the protection of the country has been stated.
notes: praṇidhi is kept untranslated (deployment of agents is the usual sense; the glossary, 5.6, keeps the sense 'agent' for notes only). The chapter title of Kangle's edition is built on this word. jana-pada = country as in the glossary.

hindi: उसके काँटों के शोधन को हम कहेंगे।
english: We shall state its cleansing of thorns.
notes: tasya most likely refers back to the country (jana-pada) of unit 1. kaṇṭaka-śodhana ('cleansing of thorns') is the name of this Book; no sense beyond the literal one is added.

words.gloss: liquor-seller (word broken at the line end)
words.gram: dvandva member; begins here, ends in next token

words.gloss: agents in the guise of (all the foregoing)

hindi: समाहर्ता जनपद में सिद्ध, तपस्वी, प्रव्रजित, चक्रचर, चारण, ठग, प्रच्छन्दक, कार्तान्तिक, नैमित्तिक, मौहूर्तिक, चिकित्सक, पागल, गूँगे, बहरे, जड़, अन्धे, वैदेहक, कारु, शिल्पी, कुशीलव, वेश, मद्य बेचने वाले, पुए बेचने वाले, पक्व मांस बेचने वाले और भात बेचने वाले के वेश वाले गुप्तचरों को नियुक्त करे।
english: The Collector should deploy in the country agents in the guise of holy men (siddha), ascetics, renunciants, cakra-wanderers, bards, tricksters, pracchandakas, soothsayers, omen-readers, astrologers, physicians, madmen, mutes, deaf men, dull men, blind men, traders (vaidehaka), artisans, craftsmen, kuśīlavas, veśa, liquor-sellers, cake-sellers, sellers of cooked meat and rice-sellers.

text_flags.suggest: śauṇḍika (the next token 'ka.āpūpika...' begins with the rest of the word)
text_flags.why: The word is broken across the printed line by a line-end hyphen; the join is a typesetting artefact, not an unsandhied join.

notes: One long compound (dvandva) ending in vyañjanān, so every member is given its own entry here and the case ending sits on the last; 'agents in the guise of' follows the glossary X-vyañjana. The printed '.-' at the ends of tokens 3 and 4 and 'śauṇḍi- / ka' are line breaks inside the compound. Obscure and kept untranslated: pracchandaka, kuśīlava (actor or bard in notes only, per glossary), veśa (literally 'dress' or 'dwelling'; the sense here is not certain). cakra.cara: read as one sub-compound 'cakra-wanderers'; alternative is two separate members, 'wheel-bearers' and 'wanderers'. kārtāntika = soothsayer (glossary 11.1; the 12.2 and 10.3 lines say fortune-teller, a reviewer should settle). pākva.māṃsika is given as two members 'cooked' and 'meat-seller' (translated 'sellers of cooked meat'); śauṇḍika 'liquor-seller' and cāraṇa 'bard' are the usual senses, medium confidence. vaidehaka = trader, kept in the Hindi as वैदेहक per glossary 8.4 (the English says trader).

hindi: वे गाँवों के और अध्यक्षों के शौच और अशौच को जानें।
english: They should know the purity and impurity of the villages and of the superintendents.
notes: te = the agents of unit 3. Taken literally 'of the villages and of the superintendents'; the alternative is that grāmāṇām qualifies adhyakṣāṇām (village superintendents), but the text has ca after the second word. śauca/aśauca = purity/impurity (honesty and dishonesty in the context), kept literal.

hindi: और यहाँ जिस किसी पर गुप्त आजीविका वाला होने की शंका करे, उसकी गुप्तचर से जासूसी करवाए।
english: And whomever here he may suspect of living by hidden means, him he should have spied upon by a secret agent.
notes: The token 'ca-atra' is two words (ca, atra). apasarpayet is the causative of apa-√sṛp; the exact sense of the causative with sattrin is not certain (alternatives: 'have him approached', 'send out a spy against him'). apasarpa = spy, sattrin = secret agent (glossary). gūḍha-ājīvin = one living by hidden means (a secret livelihood), kept literal.

words.gloss: one who has come to trust

hindi: विश्वास को प्राप्त हुए धर्मस्थ से गुप्तचर कहे — “यह मेरा बन्धु अभियुक्त है; उसका यह अनर्थ दूर किया जाए और यह धन स्वीकार किया जाए।”
english: The secret agent should say to the dharmastha who has come to trust [him]: "That relative of mine has been charged; let this loss of his be remedied, and let this wealth be accepted."
notes: dharmastha is kept as a term (dharmastha = judge in later usage, not imported). anartha = loss (glossary 9.7), alternative 'misfortune, trouble'; abhiyukta = charged, accused. The closing iti is carried by the closing quotation mark only. The standalone '-' is a dash. The quotation is closed.

hindi: यदि वह वैसा करे तो “उपदा लेने वाला” के रूप में निर्वासित किया जाए।
english: If he should do so, he should be banished [as] "taker of upadā".
notes: iti here marks the label ('as one called ...') and is not rendered 'thus'. upadā = gift, present (usually understood as bribe), kept literal. pravāsyeta: the glossary (11.1, 12.3) renders pravāsayet of a person as 'do away with'; here the literal causative of pra-√vas is 'send away, banish' and that is used, a reviewer should confirm.

hindi: इससे प्रदेष्टाओं की व्याख्या हो गई।
english: By this the pradeṣṭṛs are explained.
notes: pradeṣṭṛ kept as a term (glossary 5.3). The sentence means that the same rule applies to them; the text says only 'are explained'.

hindi: गाँव के कूट को या अध्यक्ष को गुप्तचर कहे — “वह दुष्ट धन से सम्पन्न है; उसका यह अनर्थ है; इसलिए इससे आहरण करवाओ।”
english: The secret agent should say to the grāma-kūṭa or to a superintendent: "That wretch has abundant wealth; this is his loss; therefore have him bring [it]."
notes: grāma-kūṭa is obscure and kept untranslated (usually taken as a village headman, unconfirmed; kūṭa can also mean 'false'). jālma = wretch, scoundrel. The object of āhārayasva is not stated (money or a payment is the likely sense, not added); the Hindi keeps the literal 'आहरण'. anartha = loss as in the glossary; 'this is his misfortune' is the alternative. tena-enam is two words. Closing iti carried by the quotation marks. The quotation is closed.

hindi: यदि वह वैसा करे तो “उत्कोचक” के रूप में निर्वासित किया जाए।
english: If he should do so, he should be banished [as] "utkocaka".
notes: utkocaka is kept as printed; from utkoca, usually understood as bribe, so 'bribe-taker', but the text gives no gloss. See unit 7 for pravāsyeta and iti.

words.gloss: by the known abundance of loss

hindi: या बनावटी रूप से अभियुक्त व्यक्ति झूठे साक्षियों के प्रति ज्ञात अनर्थ की विपुलता के साथ आरम्भ करे।
english: Or one under a feigned charge should set about the false witnesses with the known abundance of loss.
notes: Hard line, low confidence. The reading is the literal one: kṛtaka = artificial, feigned (the agent charged only as a pretence is the likely sense, not stated); kūṭa-sākṣin taken as the object of ārabheta; abhijñāta-anartha-vaipulya (known, loss, abundance) as an instrumental, possibly 'by [their] recognised great loss' or 'by the known extent of harm', the construction is uncertain. Alternatives: kūṭa-sākṣiṇaḥ as nominative, 'false witnesses ...'. 'ārabheta' may mean 'set about' or 'take hold of'.

hindi: यदि वे वैसा करें तो “झूठे साक्षी” के रूप में निर्वासित किए जाएँ।
english: If they should do so, they should be banished [as] "false witnesses".
notes: See unit 7 for pravāsyeran and iti.

hindi: इससे झूठी घोषणा करने वालों की व्याख्या हो गई।
english: By this the makers of false announcements are explained.
notes: kūṭa-śrāvaṇa = false causing-to-hear (announcement, declaration); the exact practice is not stated, so the literal sense is kept. Medium confidence on 'announcements'.

hindi: अथवा जिसे मन्त्र, योग, मूलकर्म या श्माशानिक कर्मों से संवदन करने वाला माने, उससे गुप्तचर कहे — “अमुक की पत्नी, पुत्रवधू या पुत्री को मैं चाहता हूँ; वह मुझे भी चाहे; और यह धन स्वीकार किया जाए।”
english: Or whomever he may think to be one who brings about winning-over (saṃvadana) by mantras, contrivances, root-actions or by cremation-ground [rites], to him the secret agent should say: "I desire the wife, the daughter-in-law or the daughter of so-and-so; let her desire me in return, and let this wealth be accepted."

text_flags.why: possible short vowel for kāraka (unit 15 reads saṃvadana.kāraka)

notes: The standalone '-' is a dash. saṃvadana is rendered 'winning-over' (cf. glossary 12.2 sāṃvadanikī oṣadhī = love-winning herb); no further sense added. yoga = contrivance (glossary 12.4 with mantra); mūla-karman = root-action, literal; śmāśānikaiḥ is taken as an adjective agreeing with karmabhiḥ ('[rites]' bracketed), alternatively a separate noun 'by the people of the cremation ground'. The accusative saṃvadana-karakam is spelt 'karaka' in the e-text, read as kāraka (see the next unit), possible typo. Closing iti carried by the quotation marks; the quotation is closed.

hindi: यदि वह वैसा करे तो “संवदन करने वाला” के रूप में निर्वासित किया जाए।
english: If he should do so, he should be banished [as] "one who brings about winning-over" (saṃvadana-kāraka).
notes: See unit 14 for saṃvadana and unit 7 for pravāsyeta and iti.

words.gloss: two whose practice is kṛtya and abhicāra

hindi: इससे कृत्य और अभिचार के अभ्यासी दोनों की व्याख्या हो गई।
english: By this the two [kinds of person] whose practice is kṛtya and abhicāra are explained.
notes: kṛtya and abhicāra are kept as terms (spell-working and rites against someone, no sense imported). The dual is read as two kinds of person, kṛtya-śīla and abhicāra-śīla; the bracket supplies 'kinds of person'. Note kṛtya here is not the kṛtya of kṛtya-pakṣa (glossary 12.3).

words.gloss: one dealing in medicines and food

hindi: अथवा जिसे विष का बनाने वाला, खरीदने वाला, बेचने वाला, या औषधि और भोजन का व्यवहार करने वाला, विष देने वाला माने, उससे गुप्तचर कहे — “वह मेरा शत्रु है; उसका उपघात किया जाए; और यह धन स्वीकार किया जाए।”
english: Or whomever he may think to be a poisoner (rasada), a maker, buyer or seller of poison, or one dealing in medicines and food, to him the secret agent should say: "That one is my enemy; let injury to him be done, and let this wealth be accepted."
notes: rasa = poison and rasada = poisoner follow the glossary (12.2, 5.2). The standalone '-' is a dash. vyavahārin = one who deals in or trades; whether 'medicines and food' are poisoned is not stated. upaghāta = injury, literal. Closing iti carried by the quotation marks; the quotation is closed.

hindi: यदि वह वैसा करे तो “विष देने वाला” के रूप में निर्वासित किया जाए।
english: If he should do so, he should be banished [as] "poisoner" (rasada).
notes: See unit 7 for pravāsyeta and iti; rasada = poisoner (glossary 5.2).

hindi: इससे मदन-योग का व्यवहार करने वाले की व्याख्या हो गई।
english: By this the dealer in madana compounds is explained.
notes: madana is kept as a name and its effect is not stated (glossary 14.1, 14.4); yoga = compound there. For Book 4 a reviewer should settle compound versus preparation versus contrivance.

words.gloss: of charcoal, ash, asandaṃśa, muṣṭika, anvil, bimba, ṭaṅka and crucibles
having as mark hands and clothes smeared with soot, ash and smoke
in contact with a smith's implements

hindi: अथवा जिसे विविध धातुओं और क्षारों का, कोयले, राख, असन्दंश, मुष्टिक, निहाई, बिम्ब, टङ्क और मूषाओं का बार-बार खरीदने वाला, कालिख, राख और धुएँ से सने हाथ और वस्त्र के चिह्न वाला, लोहार के उपकरणों से सम्पर्क रखने वाला, खोटे सिक्के बनाने वाला माने, उसके पास गुप्तचर शिष्यभाव से और व्यवहार से प्रवेश पाकर उसे ज्ञात करा दे।
english: Or whomever he may think to be a maker of false coins, a frequent buyer of various metals and alkalis and of charcoal, ash, asandaṃśa, muṣṭika, anvils, bimba, ṭaṅka and crucibles, bearing the mark of hands and clothes smeared with soot, ash and smoke, in contact with a smith's implements, him the secret agent, having entered upon him by pupilhood and by dealings, should make known.

text_flags.why: possible: the a- looks odd; sandaṃśa 'pincers, tongs' is the expected tool name in a smith's list

notes: Long phrase of obscure tool names; asandaṃśa, muṣṭika, bimba, ṭaṅka are kept untranslated (glossary rule for obscure words), 'anvil' for adhikaraṇī and 'crucible' for mūṣā are the usual senses; maṣī = soot (also ink). nānā may govern only loha ('various metals') or both. kūṭa-rūpa = false coin (glossary 5.2). The object taṃ is taken with anupraviśya and prajñāpayet; prajñāpayet = causative of pra-√jñā, 'make known' (next unit: prajñātaḥ), the exact sense (discover, expose) is not added. ca-anupraviśya is two words.

hindi: ज्ञात हो जाने पर “खोटे सिक्के बनाने वाला” के रूप में निर्वासित किया जाए।
english: Once made known, he should be banished [as] "maker of false coins".
notes: See unit 7 for pravāsyeta and iti.

hindi: इससे राग का अपहरण करने वाला और खोटे सोने का व्यवहार करने वाला, दोनों की व्याख्या हो गई।
english: By this the remover of rāga (colour) and the dealer in false gold are explained.
notes: rāgasya-apahartā is two words. rāga = colour, dye (possibly the colour or lustre of gold; the text does not say), kept literal. The singular vyākhyātaḥ agrees with the nearest subject (or the two are one person); the Hindi and English give both.

hindi: किन्तु हिंसा में आरम्भ करने वाले, गुप्त आजीविका वाले तेरह निर्वासित किए जाएँ, या अपराध की विशेषता के अनुसार निष्क्रय के लिए दें।
english: But the thirteen living by hidden means who begin [acts] of violence are to be banished, or should give for the purpose of redemption, according to the particular offence.
notes: Anuṣṭubh, 16 syllables per line, no metre problem. Object of dadyuḥ is not stated and not supplied. ārabdhāraḥ hiṃsāyām = those who begin (acts) in violence; whether the 'thirteen' are the classes of the preceding units is not stated (a reviewer may count). niṣkraya = redemption (payment in lieu), literal.
